The general idea is something I would want, however it has to be cleared up that VRChat doesn't do instance servers, it has relay servers and the "locally hosted" option would just be walking back to how VRChat worked before.

The relay servers were introduced because of security and because dealing with that many p2p connections (directly connecting to everyone, individually, instead of just one connection to the relay server) is quite intense on people's networks and computers.

However, I would want this to be a thing, it would just need a warning window when joining an instance like that and it should probably be "invite only".

details:
I live in Australia, where the closest servers are located in Japan. To play with someone who lives in the same country, it still means that (when connected to a Japanese server with really good internet mind you - I'm using a Gigabit ethernet connection with extremely low latency) I still have 180ms of ping. It's closer to 300ms on any other server location - which is 90% of the time.

With just two people, it means that at minimum the round trip is excruciatingly long - constantly desyncing in video worlds and talking over each other. And it gets worse with more people.

I think that it would benefit those of us who live far away from servers to create an option to make a localhost connection for an instance; whereby the instance owner hosts server on their system - in a fashion similar to Minecraft Bedrock Edition's online multiplayer features. 

It could be placed alongside the other server options when making a new instance; and maybe there could be either an automatic limit on how many users those locally-hosted instances could have, or a user-adjusted one based on hardware that could be altered in the in game settings or when setting up the instance. 

But it would be up to the individual users to decide who should host it; based on internet speed and latency and overall performance of their system. I understand that this would be tricky to mandate; especially with the extremely varied internet speeds that people have. But I think it could be a vital way to bring latency and other sync-related issues down. This could perhaps be a PC-exclusive feature if system performance and internet speeds were a concern.
title: Locally Hosted instances
